# Provider fixtures

Responses the injected HTTP transport replays in tests. The `openai/` files are hand-written from OpenAI's documented response shapes, not captured from live calls; replace them with real captures (Credentials removed) during the live smoke test (#11).

The OpenAI error responses (`invalid-api-key`, `insufficient-quota`, `billing-hard-limit-reached`, `rate-limit-exceeded`, `moderation-blocked`, `content-policy-violation`, `server-error`, `invalid-value`) follow OpenAI's documented `{ "error": { "message", "type", "param", "code" } }` shape; the tests pair each with the HTTP status OpenAI sends it with. `edits.json` answers `/images/edits`, which responds in the same shape as `/images/generations`.

The `gemini/` files are likewise hand-written, from Google's Interactions API docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation, https://ai.google.dev/api/interactions-api and https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-errors), not captured from live calls; replace them during the live smoke test (#11). `interaction.json` is a completed Interaction whose `thought` step carries an interim image (which litevision must ignore) before the `model_output` step with the final image. `interaction-blocked.json` is a safety block delivered as HTTP 200 (`status: "failed"`, `errors[].code: "image_safety"`); `interaction-text-only.json` is a completed Interaction with text and no image. `invalid-argument.json` is a made-up 400 naming the `response_format.image_size` field it rejects. The HTTP errors use the Interactions `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }` shape, except `api-key-invalid.json`, which uses Google's older `{ "error": { "code", "message", "status", "details" } }` shape with reason `API_KEY_INVALID`, as `/models` answers. `models.json` and `models-page-2.json` are two pages of `GET /models`, linked by `nextPageToken`.

The `apimart/` files are hand-written from APIMart's official docs (https://docs.apimart.ai/en), also not live captures; #11 replaces them. Sources:

- `submitted.json`, and the `{ "error": { "code", "message", "type" } }` errors `invalid-api-key` (401), `insufficient-balance` (402) and `rate-limit` (429): the response examples on the GPT-Image-2 page (`api-reference/images/gpt-image-2/generation`).
- `task-*.json`: Get Task Status (`api-reference/tasks/status`). `task-completed.json` follows its documented example, where `result.images[].url` is an array; `pending`, `processing`, `failed` and `cancelled` keep that shape with the fields the page lists for each status. The moderation message in `task-failed-moderation.json` is made up; the page documents only the `error` object's fields. So is the message of `invalid-parameter.json` (400), which names the `resolution` option it rejects.
- `models.json`: Models List Metadata (`api-reference/texts/models/list`) with `expand=category`.
- `schema-gpt-image-2.json`: that page says `GET /v1/models/{model}/schema` answers in the same shape as one list item with `expand=parameters`. Its `input_schema` is filled in from the GPT-Image-2 page's request fields.

The `venice/` files are hand-written from Venice's API reference and OpenAPI spec (https://docs.venice.ai, `https://api.venice.ai/doc/api/swagger.yaml`), not captured from live calls; replace them during #11 too. `models-image.json` and `models-inpaint.json` answer `GET /models?type=image` and `?type=inpaint`, with one model of each sizing style: `widthHeightDivisor` above 1 (`venice-sd35`, sized in pixels), `aspectRatios` only (`qwen-image-2`), and `aspectRatios` plus `resolutions` (`nano-banana-pro`); the edit models carry `maxInputImages` or `combineImages: false`. `generate*.json` answer `/image/generate`, including a partial result with `content_policy_violation_count`. The error files follow Venice's documented `{ "error", "code" }` shape; the tests pair each with its HTTP status. `invalid-request.json` (400) follows the spec's `DetailedError` shape, `{ "error", "details" }`, with the field errors under `details`. `/image/edit` and `/image/multi-edit` answer with raw image bytes, so the tests reply with a PNG directly.

The `together/` files are live captures from Together AI (November 2026, Credential removed), except where noted. `models.json` is six entries of `GET /v1/models`, which answers with a bare array: one chat and one audio model (litevision must leave them out), two image and two video models. `images.json` is a real `/v1/images/generations` answer with `response_format: "base64"`, its image swapped for the 1×1 PNG. `invalid-api-key.json` (401), `model-not-available.json` (404), `passthrough-blocked.json` (403, `third_party_data_sharing_blocked`) and `invalid-reference-image.json` (400, the answer to a reference image sent as bare base64 rather than a data URL) are the images API's errors as captured. `video-submitted.json` and `video-completed.json` are a real Wan 2.7 job from `POST /v2/videos` and `GET /v2/videos/{id}`, with `seconds` set to 5 and the result's short link replaced; Together's answer carries neither the video's size nor its cost. `video-failed.json` is hand-written from the failure shape in Together's docs (`error.code` such as `invalidDuration`). The video API answers a rejected Credential with the plain text `invalid api key`, which the tests send directly.
